subject: Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions

messages.author: 72125f28a2ababcd
messages.subject: Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions
parts:
Hello all,

I am new to Nimble and I would really appreciate it if someone can provide any suggestions here.

So I am trying to run an integrated model in Nimble where I am using two sub-models based on two different data sources.

My code is pasted below. Both BBS and CIP model runs fine on their own. But running this integrated model goes in a loop with "Warning: slice sampler reached the maximum number of contractions for N_BBS[1694], Current parameter value is 3."

I get that it has something to do with N_BBS, maybe its prior? But I am not sure.

Can anyone please look at my code and explain to me what am I doing wrong?

That will be really helpful.

Thanks,
IP

Code:
abundancemodel_combined<- nimbleCode({
 
  # Integrated Covariate
  alpha1 ~ dunif(-3,3)    # integrated covariate
 
  # BBS Model
  for(i in 1:nSites_BBS){
    log(lambda_BBS[i]) <- alpha0_BBS + alpha1 * cov_BBS[i]
    N_BBS[i] ~ dpois(lambda_BBS[i])
    for(t in 1:nVisits_BBS){
      logit(p_BBS[i,t]) <- beta0_BBS + alpha1_BBSnoise_BBS[i,t] + alpha2_BBSwind_BBS[i]
      y_BBS[i,t] ~ dbin(p_BBS[i,t], N_BBS[i])
    }
  }
  alpha0_BBS ~ dunif(-3,3)
  beta0_BBS ~ dunif(-3,3)
  beta1_BBS ~ dunif(-3,3)
  beta2_BBS ~ dunif(-3,3)

  # CIP Model
  for(i in 1:nSites_CIP){
    log(lambda_CIP[i]) <- alpha0_CIP + alpha1 * cov_CIP[i]
    N_CIP[i] ~ dpois(lambda_CIP[i])
   
    for(v in 1:nVisits_CIP[i]){
      logit(p_CIP[i,v]) <- beta0_CIP + beta1_CIPnoise_CIP[i,v] + beta2_CIPwind_CIP[i,v]
      y_CIP[i,v] ~ dbin(p_CIP[i,v], N_CIP[i])
     
    }
  }
  alpha0_CIP ~ dunif(-3,3)
  beta0_CIP ~ dunif(-3,3)
  beta1_CIP ~ dunif(-3,3)
  beta2_CIP ~ dunif(-3,3)
 
})

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions
parts:
Dear Igloo Pigloo,

Are there missing multiplication signs in your code?  E.g. should "alpha1_BBSnoise_BBS[i,t]" be "alpha1_BBS * noise_BBS[i,t]" ???

The error you are getting usually arises if a slice sampler is trying to update a node in the model that it is really impossible to update because of some invalid values.  This could occur, for example, due to one of the binomial declarations.  For example, if you have N_BBS[i] < y_BBS[i, y], the binomial log probability will be -Inf, and the sampler will be confused.  Normally this would only occur as a result of invalid initial values.  The first thing I would check is if your initial values are complete and valid.  Also, please be sure to update nimble.  We did just put a new version on CRAN that fixes a bug introduced in a short-lived recent version; that bug has to do with posterior predictive sampling in some cases, which doesn't look like it would be the problem in your model, but anyway please update for good measure.

If you can't fix the problem by ironing out initial values, please send a fully reproducible example.  Problems like this often have to do with specific data values and initial values, so just reading code is not sufficient to see what the problem is.

Perry

Best,
